nodes.label: AskUserQuestion Harness Binding
nodes.rationale: The one place that binds the harness-neutral structured-question contract to a concrete mechanism: the fenced question spec maps 1:1 onto AskUserQuestion fields (prompt/header/multiSelect/options label+description). Keeping the binding in a single annex is what lets the protocol and stage files stay harness-neutral. Harness specifics live here too: the approval gate's next-stage placeholder is rendered verbatim from the directive's next_stage field (Complete workflow when null) and never guessed, and the user's selection is recorded as the exact option label.

nodes.label: Never Echo the question Spec
nodes.rationale: A question fence is input to the tool, never output to render, and echoing it is a protocol violation rather than a style choice: it produces a wall of text the user cannot click, loses the tool's built-in Other escape, and is inconsistent with every correct rendering in the same session. Applies to every structured-question site - approval gates, interaction-mode choice, the ladder prompt, halt-and-ask, summary confirmation, the learnings gate. Fences in framework documentation are authoring specs, not chat output, so they legitimately remain.

nodes.label: Consolidated-Summary Checkpoint Rendering
nodes.rationale: Two semantic options with no A/B file-letter prefixes, presented as its own turn that ENDS: a lettered, numbered, bare-letter or self-selected answer is invalid, so the letter and description are stripped before writing. On Request changes the conductor asks what should change and ends the turn again, refusing to touch any answer until that feedback arrives, then resets the tag and re-presents. No artifact is generated until the file holds the explicit answer and the receipt command succeeds.

nodes.label: Question Batching Limits
nodes.rationale: Max four questions per call, max four options per question, and at least two options - a one-option call is rejected by the tool before the user can answer. Five or more options are split across calls (A-D, then E+) while the questions file retains the full option set as the authoritative record.

nodes.label: Built-in Other Escape
nodes.rationale: Because AskUserQuestion always offers Other, an explicit Other option must NOT be added to interactive batches - while questions files still end every question with 'X. Other (please specify)' per protocol, since the file format is harness-neutral and cannot rely on a harness affordance.
